title: Command Execution and Environment Trust
platform_conditions: POSIX process semantics (fork/exec, /bin/sh via system/popen); PATH resolution and env inheritance are Unix-specific behaviors
security_mechanism: system() and popen() hand the string to /bin/sh -c, so shell syntax in the input starts additional commands. exec-family calls avoid the shell but inherit two trust channels from their caller: PATH lookup — execvp/execvp-style calls resolve a bare command name against the current PATH, which a less-privileged child or the invoking user may have re-pointed — and the environment block, whose LD_PRELOAD/IFS values the spawned program may honor. Privilege-drop ordering is the third channel: if the code execs or opens files before dropping privileges (or drops only the effective uid while the saved uid remains root), the child inherits privileges the input may steer.

source_sink_clues.source: Request or protocol data that reaches the command string or argv, plus the inherited process environment when the caller runs privileged.
source_sink_clues.sink: system()/popen() with any interpolated content; execv/execl/execvp with attacker-influenced argv or before privilege cleanup

tracking_guards: Prefer execve with an absolute executable path and a constructed argv over system(); check that the environment passed to exec is sanitized (fixed minimal envp) when dropping privileges, that privilege irreversibly drops (setuid(getuid()) plus saved-id clearing) before any exec or file open, and that argv elements cannot be interpreted as options by the target program.
not_candidate_when: The command string is entirely constant with no external input, argv is a fixed program path with only allowlisted arguments, or the process has already dropped all privileges and the child cannot influence anything the parent trusts.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
SEI CERT C Coding Standard: ENV33-C (no system() when an exec family call suffices), ENV03-C (sanitize environment)
